name: Eldad and Medad
charge: Prophesying in the camp when the spirit rested on them, and being defended by Moses
summary: Moses told the Lord he was not able to bear the people alone, so the Lord took of the spirit that was on him and put it on seventy elders, and they prophesied. Two of the written men stayed in the camp, and the spirit rested on them there, and they prophesied in the camp. Joshua asked Moses to forbid them; Moses corrected the envy and wished that all the Lord’s people were prophets.
offenseFull: Moses said he was not able to bear all this people alone, because it was too heavy for him, and the Lord told him to gather seventy men of the elders of Israel, men he knew to be elders and officers over them, and bring them to the tabernacle; He would take of the spirit that was on Moses and put it on them, so that they would bear the burden of the people with him (Numbers 11:14-17). The spirit on the head is meant to come down to the men under him. Leadership still works that way, and the teaching says so plainly: the deacons, the captains and the officers teach the way they teach because of what was taught to them and because the spirit on the man over them was put on them, not because any one of them worked it out on his own. That is why the leaders have to be right according to the scriptures, since it is their spirit the Most High takes and lets rest on the others.

The Lord came down in a cloud, took of the spirit that was on Moses and gave it to the seventy elders, and when the spirit rested on them they prophesied and did not cease (Numbers 11:24-27): they taught, and they did not stop. It was the same with Elijah and Elisha, when Elisha asked for a double portion of his master’s spirit before Elijah was taken up and the sons of the prophets said that the spirit of Elijah rested on Elisha (2 Kings 2:9, 15), and the same in the time of Christ, when men could tell that spirit was on the apostles. But two of the men remained in the camp, Eldad and Medad, and the spirit rested on them; they were among those written, but had not gone out to the tabernacle, and they prophesied in the camp. They prophesied where the people were, not at the tabernacle with the rest, and they did not conceal it or wait for permission before speaking.
judgmentFull: A young man ran and told Moses, and Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses and one of his young men, asked Moses to forbid them (Numbers 11:28-29). Joshua was carrying a spirit of envy, and Moses corrected it: he asked whether Joshua envied for his sake, and wished that all the Lord’s people were prophets and that the Lord would put His spirit on them. The Most High wants all His people to be prophets. Do not envy the gift on another brother or sister; glean from it. A brother may be the better teacher and a sister the better labourer, so go and learn from them rather than rolling in envy. Christ answered John the same way when John forbade a man casting out devils because he did not follow with them: forbid him not, for the man who is not against us is for us (Luke 9:49-50).

The teaching reads Joshua’s word a second way as well. He was the servant of Moses, being moulded and trained to lead, and he never once tried to overthrow him; he was not vainglorious, he was loyal, and his concern was for his master and not for himself. What he saw in the camp Moses had not seen as yet, because a man can carry the spirit and still teach the scriptures for vainglory and for preeminence, which is what the seventy princes would show soon enough. The lesson drawn for a man waiting on his own ministry is the same: learn to be a disciple first, hold post, hand out a flyer, learn to read, and then learn to teach, the way Elisha would not leave his master’s side. So the blessing was defended by the one man whose standing it might have threatened, and what Moses wished for is what Joel prophesied and Peter cited at Pentecost as fulfilled: the spirit poured out on all flesh, with sons and daughters prophesying (Joel 2:28; Acts 2:16-18).

text.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, Gather unto me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom thou knowest to be the elders of the people, and officers over them; and bring them unto the tabernacle of the congregation, that they may stand there with thee.

And I will come down and talk with thee there: and I will take of the spirit which is upon thee, and will put it upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with thee, that thou bear it not thyself alone.
And Moses went out, and told the people the words of the Lord, and gathered the seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them round about the tabernacle.

And the Lord came down in a cloud, and spake unto him, and took of the spirit that was upon him, and gave it unto the seventy elders: and it came to pass, that, when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease.

But there remained two of the men in the camp, the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the spirit rested upon them; and they were of them that were written, but went not out unto the tabernacle: and they prophesied in the camp.
And there ran a young man, and told Moses, and said, Eldad and Medad do prophesy in the camp.
And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses, one of his young men, answered and said, My lord Moses, forbid them.
And Moses said unto him, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord’s people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit upon them!

And it came to pass, when they were gone over, that Elijah said unto Elisha, Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken away from thee. And Elisha said, I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me.
And when the sons of the prophets which were to view at Jericho saw him, they said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha. And they came to meet him, and bowed themselves to the ground before him.
And John answered and said, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name; and we forbad him, because he followeth not with us.
And Jesus said unto him, Forbid him not: for he that is not against us is for us.
And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions:
But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel;

And it shall come to pass in the last days, saith God, I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams:
And on my servants and on my handmaidens I will pour out in those days of my Spirit; and they shall prophesy:
